values.note: Sites 1-19 are drive-in; 20-31 are tent-only, up a hill from the road (car or motorcycle parking only, no trailers or rooftop tents). values.note: Early May to late September, weather dependent; services may be missing early and late in the season.

values.note: Reserve on recreation.gov or 877-444-6777 at least four days ahead; some sites are first-come and must be occupied the first night. The Forest Service page says Friday+Saturday is required on weekends and three nights on holiday weekends (walk-ups exempt), but recreation.gov's rules set no minimum. Reservation season 2026 May 15 - Sept 19 (2027: May 14 - Sept 18), with first-come weeks either side.

values.note: Senior and Access passes: 50% off at this concessionaire-run campground, only the site the pass holder occupies.

note: San Carlos Ranger District campground strung along Ophir Creek in a narrow canyon on FSR 361, just off CO-165 north of Lake Isabel (west of Wetmore), ~8,800 ft, past a private campground at the turnoff. Sites 1-19 take trailers/RVs; 20-31 are walk-up tent sites. A trail behind site 22 leads a mile to a small waterfall; Bishop's Castle is 4 miles away. --Claude
summary: FS page + rec.gov + catalog: confirmed 31 sites (20-31 tent-only), $25, no hookups, vault toilets, hand-pump water, reservable on recreation.gov. Added max 40 (catalog), season wording (early May - late Sept), fcfs some_sites, 4-day cutoff, 14-night limit, reservation season 05-15..09-19, extra-vehicle fee, senior/access 50%. flags: Phone: stored 719-489-2034 is recreation.gov's 'facility specific information' line (the concessionaire's; recreation.gov contact lstewart@goexplorus.com). The ranger district's number, on the FS page and as recreation.gov's facility phone, is San Carlos Ranger District 719-269-8500 (3028 East Main Street, Cañon City). Suggest 719-269-8500.
Website holds two URLs on two lines (recreation.gov + the FS page); the FS page https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/ophir-creek-campground is live and the agency's.

Season conflict: FS 'open early May to late September, weather dependent'; recreation.gov's overview still says 'usually open Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day weekend with full service and ... through the middle of October with reduced service'. Recorded the FS wording.

Minimum stay conflict: FS page requires Friday+Saturday on weekends and 3 nights on holiday weekends (walk-ups exempt); recreation.gov rules for 10040622 set minWeekendStay 0 and minHolidayWeekendStay 0. Not recorded, as at Molly Brown (2410) and Father Dyer (2412).

Length: neither FS nor recreation.gov states a maximum. The catalog is sparse - RV equipment only at sites 3 (40 ft), 5, 18, 19 (32 ft); 18 of the 30 catalog sites list Tent only, including drive-in sites below 20. Recorded 40. At least four sites take a 23-ft rig.

Road: FS directions only - 'turn left onto Forest Service Road 360. Travel about 100 feet and then turn left onto Forest Service Road 361. Continue past a private campground and travel 1/2 mile'; no surface, RV or clearance wording (OSM tags the campground road gravel).

Closure order nearby, not the campground: PSICC 'Reduced Aspen Acres Fire closure order' 02-12-03-26-43 (Oct 23 - Dec 31, 2026, San Carlos RD) closes Davenport Campground, FSR 382/327 and trails including 1384 (Squirrel Creek) and 1388 (Middle Creek); Ophir Creek Campground and FSR 360/361 are not named. Its season is over anyway.

Waterfront (stored not waterfront): the campground road follows Ophir Creek (a small stream, 'creekside' vocabulary) for ~700 m, within ~10-30 m of it on OSM, but the canyon floor is under continuous conifer canopy and the catalog has no per-site coordinates, so the pads' distance to the creek can neither be confirmed nor vetoed. Agency pages only say 'Fishing in Ophir Creek'. Left as stored; re-audit lead only if wanted.

Pin 38.06001,-105.10749 sits ~60 m west of the campground road midway down the canyon; the FS coordinate 38.06249,-105.10473 (on the road near the north end) is ~370 m away and OSM's campground node 38.06142,-105.10543 ~240 m. Within 500 m; no per-site points to centre on.
